name: An old promise returns
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: At the gate, let Mara recognize the missing compass and choose what to risk to recover it.
criteria: Recognizes the compass as the ferryman’s daughter’s property, not her own.
Advances the promise through an action with a cost.
Does not claim the compass was already returned.

episodes.summary: Mara promised the ferryman she would return his daughter’s brass compass.
A toll collector refused passage without a copper.
Mara traded her blanket for passage.
Ivo spotted a brass compass on a guard’s belt.

promises.description: Return the ferryman’s daughter’s brass compass.

name: Plans are not events
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Write the moment Mara finally returns the compass in chapter 6.
criteria: The promised chapter-4 payoff did not happen.
The return occurs now and has an observable recipient.
The delay has emotional consequences.

episodes.summary: Mara promised to return the compass.
Mara reached the ferry too late. The ferryman had left, and she kept the compass.
Mara found the ferryman repairing a boat.

name: A promise reopens
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: At the ferry, face the consequences of the reopened debt.
criteria: Acknowledges the debt was settled once.
The new obligation arises from the later loss.
Does not repeat the old repayment as though it never happened.

episodes.summary: Mara borrowed a boat and promised to return it.
Mara returned the boat intact; the ferryman released her debt.
Mara borrowed it again and broke its rudder. She promised repairs.

promises.description: Mara owes the ferryman a working boat.

name: A historical viewpoint
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Write chapter 4 from Ivo’s viewpoint. He investigates the stolen toll money without knowing the culprit.
criteria: Ivo cannot know Lysa stole the money until chapter 7.
Suspicion is distinguished from knowledge.
No narrator aside reveals the future culprit.

episodes.summary: Ivo counts toll money for the ferryman.
The strongbox is found empty.
Ivo finds a torn green sleeve, but several travellers wear green.
Lysa confesses privately to Mara that she stole the toll money.

name: Power has a price
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Mara needs to cross the river, but cannot pay another magical toll. Give her a consequential solution.
criteria: No free magic or unexplained restored voice.
Mara cannot speak until tomorrow.
The solution follows a physical or interpersonal alternative.

episodes.summary: Every ferry charm costs the speaker their voice until the next dawn.
Mara used a charm at noon. Her voice vanished; it is now evening.

rules: A ferry charm consumes the speaker’s voice until the next dawn. A voiceless person cannot invoke another charm.

name: Distinct comic voices
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Write an argument over who should carry the leaking bucket, preserving both voices and affection.
criteria: Mara is terse and literal; Ivo elaborates ridiculous practical excuses.
Humour comes from their conflict and choices.
Neither voice collapses into identical polished banter.

episodes.summary: Mara answered the boatman in clipped literal sentences. Ivo invented a lengthy excuse involving a very respectable goose.
They must carry a leaking bucket uphill before the bell rings.

name: A quiet satisfying ending
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: End the episode after the rescue, with emotional satisfaction and a reason to return tomorrow.
criteria: Resolves the immediate rescue.
Does not invent a sudden attacker solely for a cliffhanger.
Leaves relational anticipation without withholding the rescue outcome.

episodes.summary: Mara and Ivo pull a child from the flooded ditch.
The child is safe at the station. Ivo has not told Mara why the child’s name affected him.

name: Revision without forgetting
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Continue after the corrected flood account; make Ivo’s changed trust visible.
criteria: Uses the corrected account: Mara stayed with Ivo.
Does not revive the abandoned version where she fled alone.
Trust changes through behaviour, not a detached recap.

episodes.summary: Corrected accepted account: Mara stayed through the flood and helped Ivo across. The earlier abandoned draft where she fled alone is not canon.
Ivo quietly hands Mara the map, letting her choose the route for the first time.

name: Return after a long hiatus
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Begin the new arc with a scene that orients a returning reader without dumping the whole series history.
criteria: Establishes the current place and immediate need.
Recalls the relevant unpaid favour naturally.
Preserves room for new action instead of summarizing every prior episode.

episodes.summary: Mara owes the miller a favour for hiding Ivo.
The miller asks for help before the spring thaw.
After winter apart, Mara and Ivo reunite beside the iced millrace.

promises.description: Repay the miller’s favour before the thaw.

name: A consequence across books
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Open book two at the border. Carry the damage and relationship change from the previous book.
criteria: Mara’s hand remains injured.
Ivo knows she burned the map to save him.
The lost map creates a practical obstacle.

episodes.summary: Mara burns their map to distract the guards.
Ivo escapes, then sees Mara’s blistered hand.
They reach the border without a map; Ivo thanks her without making a joke.

name: Promises after 200 chapters
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: At Southwatch, let Mara act on recognizing the brass compass while facing the immediate hunger problem.
criteria: Remembers the chapter-1 promise to the ferryman.
Continues from Southwatch with no food and Mara’s torn left boot.
Does not return to the burned ferry or invent food supplies.

episodes.summary: Expanded by the deterministic 200-chapter synopsis fixture.

promises.description: Return the ferryman’s daughter’s brass compass.

name: Reader concern becomes a real revision
contract: An intimate river-road fantasy. Choices have material costs; dialogue stays concrete and lightly wry.
task: Revise the chapter’s repeated bargaining pattern so failure changes Mara’s next choice, while keeping the key unbought.
criteria: The key remains unbought.
The failed bargain forces a different next action.
Avoids merely swapping adjectives or appending an unrelated hook.

episodes.summary: Mara bargains for the key and fails. She tries again with the same offer.
Accepted editorial direction: keep the key unbought, but make this failed bargain force Mara to ask the ferryman she has been avoiding for help.
